summary.headline: Poly Medicure H1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 31% to INR1,106 crore; standalone EBITDA margin guidance raised to 26%-27.5%.
summary.overview: Standalone H1 revenue grew 15% to INR919 crore with domestic up about 19-20% and international up 12.5%, while Q2 standalone revenue rose 17% to INR488 crore. Consolidated Q2 revenue was INR581 crore (up 31%, including acquisitions), with organic consolidated H1 growth of 14%. Management said gross margin pressure from West Asia-driven raw material costs was largely offset by pricing, inventory management and mix, and it raised standalone EBITDA margin guidance. Subsidiary PendraCare is loss-making at EBITDA level after losing Middle East business, and Citieffe's Italian tender delays weighed on growth.

segments.name: Infusion therapy
segments.commentary: H1 revenue INR542 crore (up 11%); Q2 INR284 crore (up 12%), with domestic infusion growing 20% in both H1 and Q2.

segments.name: Orthopaedics (Citieffe)
segments.commentary: H1 INR92 crore and Q2 INR43 crore, reflecting consolidation of Citieffe; YTD organic growth about 3-4%, with Italian public tender delays the main drag.

segments.name: Renal
segments.commentary: H1 revenue INR94 crore (up 7.5%); Q2 INR51 crore (up 20%). Cumulative dialysis machine sales about 1,250 units; over 300 machines sold in H1.

segments.name: Cardiology (PendraCare)
segments.commentary: H1 INR56 crore; Q2 INR27 crore. PendraCare YTD growth about 10%, with EBITDA currently at a loss after Middle East exposure (about 20% of 2025 revenue) went to near standstill.

segments.name: Other segments (critical care, transfusion, etc.)
segments.commentary: H1 INR317 crore (up 23%); Q2 INR173 crore (up 26%). Plan 1 Health (Italy) critical care growing double digits.

segments.name: Europe (organic)
segments.commentary: Q2 organic growth close to 40%; H1 up 29%. Consolidated India and Europe grew 19% and 29% respectively in H1.

segments.name: Rest of World (organic)
segments.commentary: Q2 down 7%; H1 down 1.8%, attributed to West Asia conflict, freight and container constraints.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated FY27 revenue guidance maintained at INR2,300-2,400 crore.
Standalone FY27 revenue guidance maintained at INR1,900-1,950 crore, with domestic growing about 20% and international about 15%.
Standalone FY27 EBITDA margin guidance raised to 26%-27.5% from 25%-27%.
Consolidated FY27 EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 23%-25%.
Standalone FY27 gross margin guided at 68%-69%; consolidated gross margin expected to stay above 70%.
FY27 capex guidance unchanged at INR200-225 crore; INR124 crore spent in H1 (INR15 crore overseas).
US revenue target of USD7-8 million for FY27; longer term USD15-25 million over the next three to four years.
Infusion contribution expected to stay at 45%-50% over the next four to five years; management reiterated plan to double revenue by FY30.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 capex INR124 crore against FY27 guidance of INR200-225 crore; INR124 crore in India and INR15 crore overseas.
Management said substantial capex is under way to balance activities and capacity across plants, including expansion in orthopaedics and cardiology.
Capacity and utilisation figures were not disclosed on the call.
Three new projects with partner expected to go live in Q1, Q4 and Q1 of the next financial year, plus a third in Q3 of next FY (projects not further specified).
demand_pricing: Standalone price increases of about 4-5% taken in Q1 to pass on raw material inflation; further calibrated hikes and higher-value product mix cited.
Management said the 200-300 bps gross margin hit guided at the start of the year was mitigated.

Dialysis: Chinese dumping continues; anti-dumping application filed end-June 2026 is still pending. DGHS circular (around 22-23 October 2026) mandates single use of dialysers, which management expects to lift demand over time.
Europe: about 28-29 new customers added in H1 and about 30 new product registrations pending in European markets.
Tender-based public procurement in Italy caused delays for Citieffe; Europe TAM described as exceeding a few billion dollars.
Middle East demand remains strong per management, but container availability, Hormuz-related port issues and freight cost increases are delaying orders.

qa_highlights.question: What was organic growth in Europe and ROW, and how are PendraCare and Citieffe growing?
qa_highlights.answer: Europe organic Q2 about 40%, H1 29%; ROW down 7% in Q2 and 1.8% in H1. PendraCare YTD about 10%; Citieffe YTD about 3-4%, with Italian tender delays.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Citieffe and PendraCare growing slowly, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Citieffe's Italian tendering delays hurt growth, while outside Italy it is in line. PendraCare has a standalone high-single-digit growth potential; with synergies management expects mid-teens, with benefits from FY28 and a large OEM win from mid-CY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PendraCare move to EBITDA losses and when will margins recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material inflation and the loss of about 20% of 2025 revenue from the Middle East hit margins on a EUR10 million base. Management expects recovery in CY27/FY28 and a 3-5 year target near 20% margin for the acquired businesses.

qa_highlights.question: Size of the European and UK tender market?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the total addressable market in Europe could exceed a few billion dollars across GPOs and tenders.

qa_highlights.question: Reason for the exceptional item of INR96 million tied to a missed earnout?
qa_highlights.answer: A jointly agreed contract development project at PendraCare failed regulatory and clinical trials and was shelved, so the contingent consideration was reversed.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin split between Q1 inventory gains and RM inflation, and FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 benefited from price hikes of about 4-5% and low-cost inventory from Q4, which is now normalising. Full-year standalone gross margin guided at 68%-69%; consolidated expected at 70%-plus.

qa_highlights.question: US business status and policy risk?
qa_highlights.answer: A new 510(k) approval for an irrigation set was received; US sales are expected to reach USD7-8 million in FY27. Too early to assess post-election policy changes, with more clarity expected next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Will short-term debt rise and what drives lease liabilities?
qa_highlights.answer: Short-term debt is rising with working capital. Lease liabilities rose as subsidiaries moved to Ind AS 116 from the start of FY27. Italian subsidiary loan repayments are EUR1.5-2 million a year.

qa_highlights.question: Dialysis competition and the outlook for renal exports?
qa_highlights.answer: Competition from China persists. Renal export is planned first to Southeast Asia, with revenue dependent on 1-2 year registration cycles; India is the near-term focus given about 90% import-driven demand.

risks_watch: Outcome of anti-dumping application on Chinese dialysis products, filed end-June 2026 and still pending.
Rest-of-world (Middle East) demand weakness, freight and container constraints, and Hormuz-related shipping risks.
Citieffe Italian public tender delays and PendraCare's EBITDA losses; recovery depends on synergies and regulatory approvals taking one to three years.
Raw material and freight cost inflation tied to the West Asia conflict; gross margin guidance of 68%-69% standalone.
US policy uncertainty after the elections; management to update next quarter.
Setup costs for UK and Brazil subsidiaries weighing on consolidated EBITDA margin.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the core India and Europe business and on the standalone margin upgrade, but cautious on the Middle East, PendraCare and Citieffe, and noncommittal on US policy changes. Answers on the subsidiaries and the US were more hedged, with several timelines pushed to CY27 or FY28.
key_quotes: We have effectively mitigated that risk by proactively managing inventory, taking calibrated price hikes, and focusing on selling high-value products.
Our domestic business continues a strong growth trajectory with a growth of 22% in quarter and more than 19% for the half year.
The biggest challenge has been its exposure to Middle East.
I think this will lead to a demand, but I think it will take some time to build up.
